correctness.rationale: The support-bijection invariant is maintained indefinitely because before each move at most 2(k−1) endpoints remain used and each ground set contains at least 2k points. Every new pair needs at most two fresh endpoints. For a smaller n<2k, the explicit existential r=ceil((n+1)/2) graph-vertex pattern forces exactly n+1 hidden points: a matching for even t, or one adjacent pair and remaining disjoint pairs for odd t, with inequality constraints preventing repeated graph vertices. Thus the iff holds for all n,m,k. Orbit-game and pattern search replay pass, but finite tests are not the infinite proof.
